title: Banknote engraving

reference.grammar: image effect: a photograph reprinted as one-ink intaglio — tone as line width, crosshatch in the shadows, lines that bend with the form, a looping guilloche in smooth upper areas, one hue range kept as a second ink, paper grain
reference.read_from: canvas at 214 % (Instruction page, “Rome · terracotta accent”) and the settings panel on the Shader page; shader source not read (view-only file)

techniques.name: Tone field (the picture)

params.subject: headland with a signal tower and sheds, sea, far ridge — generated, lit from the left

res.note: source resolution as a fraction of the sheet

techniques.limits: Any RGB picture works in its place. Pictures with no smooth area above upper_v show no guilloche; pictures with no pixel inside the hue range print as one ink.
techniques.implementation: Sky, ridge, headland and sea are evaluated per pixel from seeded Perlin noise; tower, sheds and boat are drawn as flat lit/shadow faces on top. The function returns a canvas; every later technique only reads it.

techniques.name: Exposure and contrast
techniques.limits: Contrast above ~2 clips most of the sheet to paper or solid line; the swelling line then reads as a two-level threshold.
techniques.implementation: Luminance is exposed and stretched about mid-gray before it sets any line width, so paper and solid shadow are reached inside the picture, not only at its extremes.

techniques.name: Contour flow (tone-warped phase)

amp_pitches.note: phase shift in pitches at flow = 1 for a black-to-white step

techniques.limits: flow · amp_pitches · pitch must stay under ~1.5 × radius or neighboring lines fold over each other at hard edges.
techniques.implementation: A quarter-resolution copy of the picture is blurred; its luminance is added to the line phase, so lines rise over light forms and sink into dark ones. The same pass stores blurred edge energy for the guilloche mask.

techniques.name: Swelling line screen

pitch_u.note: reference: 3.2 px on its own image; 6 u resolves at plate size

techniques.limits: Under ~2.5 device px of pitch the lines alias into tone. duty_max · weight at 1 closes the shadows to solid ink and the crosshatch has nothing to cross.
techniques.implementation: Distance to the nearest line center is compared with half the tone-set width and antialiased over one device pixel. In the highlights each line is cut into dashes whose fill falls with darkness, with a hashed offset per line.

techniques.name: Shadow crosshatch
techniques.limits: start under ~0.35 puts hatch into the midtones and the picture reads as a net, not an engraving.
techniques.implementation: A second, unwarped line set whose width ramps from 0 at start to duty_max · strength at full darkness; the two sets are combined as 1 − (1−a)(1−b).

techniques.name: Guilloche in upper smooth regions

curvature.note: max slope of the wave; amplitude = curvature · scale / 2π

tone.note: how much darkness thickens the guilloche line

drift.note: phase wander of family A down the sheet

shear.note: family B phase advance per unit y, in units of 2π/S — tilts the braid so it does not stripe

params.lines: A: y + a·sin(2πx/S + drift·sin(2πy/2.3S)) = k·pitch;  B: y − a·sin(2πx/S + shear·2πy/S + 1.1) = k·pitch

techniques.limits: curvature above ~3 makes the wave steeper than the antialiasing estimate holds; pitch near the main pitch makes the hand-over at upper_v invisible.
techniques.implementation: Two families of stacked sine lines, mirrored, give the braided cells. Vertical distance is divided by √(1 + slope²) so line width stays even on the steep parts. The mask is (above upper_v) × (edge energy low); the straight lines fade by the same mask.

techniques.name: Kept hue as a second ink

params.mode: variant.accent — "hue": ink takes each pixel’s own hue · "#hex": one custom ink · "off": monochrome

techniques.limits: tolerance + feather above ~90° keys most warm pictures whole; min_sat under ~8 % keys neutral grays by their noise hue.
techniques.implementation: Mask = 1 inside tolerance of the chosen hue, feathered to 0, gated by saturation, scaled by strength and pulled back toward the main ink in the shadows by keep_shadows. It changes ink color only — line width is unchanged.

techniques.name: Paper grain

cell_u.note: grain cell; one device pixel at the default

techniques.limits: Above ~0.06 the grain reads before the line; this pass is the last thing to add and the first to remove.
techniques.implementation: One multiplicative monochrome noise pass over paper and ink together, on cells of 1.4 u with lag-1 correlation.

pass_order: picture · tone field drawn or supplied, upsampled to the sheet
field · blurred luminance + edge energy at ¼ resolution
lines · phase = y/pitch + flow field; width from darkness; dashes in the highlights
hatch · second set at 62° above 58 % darkness
guilloche · two sine families where upper and smooth; straight lines fade there
ink · kept-hue ink or main ink, composited on paper by line coverage
notes: Parameter names and values under reference.figma_panel are copied from the effect’s settings panel as shown in the file. How the effect maps them internally is not known; the functions here are a rebuild from the rendered result, not a port of its shader.
Figma’s Selected hue 52 is on its own scale (the file’s quick start gives orange ≈ 25°, green ≈ 105°, red ≈ 0°); this spec uses degrees.
Reference paper is #F5EEDD; the rebuild prints on neutral #F4F5F3 in every variant.
No reference image is bundled (third-party file); compare is off for this plate.
